workflow_yaml:
name: Jenkinsfile conversion

on:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      APP_ENV: ci
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Build
        run: ./gradlew --no-daemon clean build

      - name: Test
        id: run_tests
        run: ./gradlew --no-daemon test

      - name: Publish JUnit results
        if: ${{ always() && steps.run_tests.outcome != 'skipped' }}
        uses: dorny/test-reporter@v2
        with:
          name: JUnit Test Results
          path: build/test-results/test/*.xml
          reporter: java-junit
          fail-on-error: 'true'

      - name: Archive build artifacts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: build-artifacts
          path: build/libs/*.jar
          if-no-files-found: error
assumptions: The source specifies no trigger, so workflow_dispatch is an evaluation-only trigger assumption.
The source does not specify an agent platform or runner tooling; ubuntu-latest is a reasonable Linux runner assumption and is not claimed to match Jenkins.
The checkout action represents the explicit checkout scm step and checks out the workflow repository's source.
The sequential stages run in one GitHub Actions job so they share a workspace; the source defines no parallel stages or cross-job artifact transfer.
Jenkins fingerprinting has no direct equivalent in this workflow; the JARs are uploaded as an artifact without fingerprint tracking.

JUnit results are reported with GitHub checks/annotations and a summary rather than Jenkins' JUnit UI. The Gradle test command retains its failure status, and the report step runs after it even when it fails; missing report files are configured to fail.
The selected action versions and Ubuntu runner image are conversion choices not specified by the source.

behavior_mapping.source: Declarative pipeline environment sets APP_ENV to ci.
Test stage runs ./gradlew --no-daemon test after Build.
behavior_mapping.target: jobs.build.steps[2].run; steps execute sequentially in the same job

behavior_mapping.source: Test stage always publishes build/test-results/test/*.xml through Jenkins junit, including after test-command failure.
behavior_mapping.target: jobs.build.steps[3] uses dorny/test-reporter with the literal glob, runs after the test step unless that step was skipped, and fails on reporting errors

behavior_mapping.source: Pipeline post always archives build/libs/*.jar, including after earlier stage failures; fingerprinting is enabled.
behavior_mapping.target: jobs.build.steps[4] uploads the literal glob with if: always() and if-no-files-found: error; fingerprinting is unsupported
